method: Evidence-based adjudication of three blind primary proposals; reviewer agreement was treated as evidence rather than authority.

route.title: Dated opening word and delay claim
route.deciding_seam: Hag.1.1 supplies the date, word-event formula, named addressees, and saying introduction; Hag.1.2 supplies the introduced community claim, and a WLC-family pe follows before the renewed word event at Hag.1.3.
route.defensible_basis: The grammatical introduction is incomplete without the quoted saying it introduces. Syntactic completion, paragraph closure after 1:2, and the renewed word-event formula at 1:3 converge on a two-verse opening unit.
route.counterevidence: The date and addressee notice has a recoverable framing function and governs more than the quoted claim, but that metadata function does not outweigh its syntactic dependence.

route.title: Paneled-house accusation and futility
route.deciding_seam: The renewed word event at Hag.1.3 introduces the paneled-house accusation, consider-your-ways summons, and cumulative sowing, eating, drinking, clothing, and wages register through 1:6; a WLC-family pe follows.
rejected_alternatives: Separate chunks for individual futility outcomes
route.defensible_basis: Frame, accusation, evaluation summons, and futility consequences form one accusation-and-result oracle before the repeated speech and consider formulas at 1:7.
route.counterevidence: The divine-speech formula near the consider summons and the memorable list create internal rhetorical turns, while the repeated consider formula at 1:7 links both confrontation movements.

route.title: Building commission and drought explanation
route.deciding_seam: Repeated divine-speech and consider-your-ways formulas introduce the mountain, wood, and build commands; disappointed expectation, explanatory clauses, withheld yield, and the drought register continue through Hag.1.11, followed by a WLC-family samekh.
route.defensible_basis: Commission, failed expectation, causal explanation, and drought result are mutually dependent movements of one oracle with marked closure.
route.counterevidence: The imperative cluster at 1:8 and the expectation-and-explanation turn at 1:9 are recoverable internal movements.

route.title: Obedience, assurance, stirring, work, and date coda
route.deciding_seam: Narrated obedience begins at Hag.1.12, messenger assurance responds at 1:13, divine stirring and work continue through 1:14, and the prepositional date in 1:15 completes when the reported work occurred before the fresh dated word event at 2:1.
route.defensible_basis: The bare date phrase lacks a fresh word-event formula and is syntactically and narratively dependent on the work report. Keeping it with 1:12-14 preserves response, assurance, stirring, work, and chronology together.
route.counterevidence: The WLC-family pe after 1:14 is genuine evidence for a dependent date-coda seam, and the messenger assurance at 1:13 is a distinct embedded speech.

route.title: Former-glory question and encouragement
route.deciding_seam: The dated word event and addressee command introduce the former-glory questions, threefold be-strong and work summons, covenant and presence language, Spirit reassurance, and fear-not close; a WLC-family samekh follows Hag.2.5.
route.defensible_basis: Question, encouragement, work command, and reassurance form a complete dated encouragement movement with marked closure at 2:5.
route.counterevidence: The encouragement at 2:4 and compressed covenant-and-Spirit relation at 2:5 are internal turns, while the causal opening at 2:6 keeps this child dependent on the full 2:1-9 oracle.

route.title: Shaking, glory, and peace promise
route.deciding_seam: A renewed divine-speech formula and yet-once-more expression begin the shaking register; heavens, earth, sea, nations, valuable things, silver, gold, latter house glory, and peace continue through Hag.2.9, followed by a WLC-family pe.
route.defensible_basis: The shaking movement resolves specifically in house glory and peace; the intervening silver-and-gold statement functions within that resolution rather than starting an independent oracle.
route.counterevidence: The causal opening links backward to 2:1-5, and repeated speech formulas plus the declaration at 2:8 create internal turns.

route.title: Priestly questions and prophetic application
route.deciding_seam: The dated word event commands inquiry of the priests; the holiness-contact question and answer at Hag.2.12, corpse-impurity question and answer at 2:13, and Haggai's application to people, work, and offering at 2:14 form one instructional sequence before the retrospective summons at 2:15.
route.defensible_basis: The paired cases are deliberately asymmetrical, and the prophetic application states their literary result. Neither answer safely represents the passage without the other question and the application.
route.counterevidence: Each priestly exchange is formally complete, 2:14 changes from dialogue to application, and no WLC-family paragraph marker closes after 2:14.

route.title: Retrospective shortfall and failed return
route.deciding_seam: The first consider-from-this-day-and-backward summons introduces pre-foundation shortfall, reduced stores, blight, mildew, hail, and failed return through Hag.2.17; the consider command restarts explicitly at 2:18 with a newly specified foundation-day threshold.
rejected_alternatives: Separate chunks for individual agricultural losses
route.defensible_basis: The negative retrospective has its own summons, temporal orientation, cumulative failure register, and failed-return conclusion. The repeated command and changed temporal threshold at 2:18 are stronger than a merely stylistic internal turn.
route.counterevidence: This is the negative first half of a larger reversal whose blessing arrives only in 2:18-19; it must retain the 2:15-19 parent.

route.title: Foundation-day hinge and blessing reversal
route.deciding_seam: The repeated consider summons names the foundation-day threshold; absent seed and unproductive plants lead to the from-today blessing reversal, and a WLC-family samekh follows Hag.2.19.
route.defensible_basis: The doubled command, explicit foundation-day threshold, inventory question, reversal promise, and paragraph closure establish a coherent dependent blessing child. The evidence is not treated as tied because both form and temporal orientation restart at 2:18.
route.counterevidence: The child cannot establish the force of its reversal without the shortfall and failed-return history in 2:15-17, so isolated retrieval is prohibited by mandatory parent hydration.

route.title: Second same-day Zerubbabel oracle
route.deciding_seam: The word comes a second time on the same day at Hag.2.20; direct address to Zerubbabel develops through creation shaking, kingdom and chariot overthrow, mutual sword, servant address, signet image, election statement, and the final speech formula at 2:23.
route.defensible_basis: The explicit second-word frame, named addressee, overthrow sequence, servant-and-signet culmination, election statement, and terminal speech formula form one complete closing oracle.
route.counterevidence: Hag.2.23 changes from broad overthrow imagery to highly retrievable personal servant, signet, and election language, but it is the addressed culmination rather than an independent identity oracle.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Hag.1.1-Hag.1.2 as one surface unit.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The saying introduction in 1:1 requires the quoted message in 1:2. The pe after 1:2 and renewed word-event formula at 1:3 provide convergent closure evidence.

contested_case_rulings.case: Pe after Hag.1.14 and attachment of Hag.1.15
contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Hag.1.12-Hag.1.15 whole and preserve Hag.1.12-1.14 plus dependent date coda 1:15 as an internal alternative.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The pe is real paragraph evidence, but 1:15 is a bare chronological phrase that completes the work report and lacks a fresh word-event formula. It is too dependent to surface alone.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Surface the two children and require Hag.2.1-Hag.2.9 hydration for both.
contested_case_rulings.reason: A samekh after 2:5 and renewed divine-speech formula at 2:6 support the split, while the causal opening and former-to-latter glory movement preserve their larger dependency.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Hag.2.10-Hag.2.14 indivisible at the surface.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The two asymmetrical priestly cases and Haggai's application are one instructional form. Detaching an answer or the application would misrepresent the passage's literary logic.

contested_case_rulings.case: Whole Hag.2.15-Hag.2.19 versus Hag.2.15-2.17 and Hag.2.18-2.19
contested_case_rulings.ruling: Surface Hag.2.15-Hag.2.17 and Hag.2.18-Hag.2.19 as dependent children under the mandatory Hag.2.15-Hag.2.19 parent.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The evidence is not tied: Hag.2.18 repeats the consider command and adds an explicit foundation-day temporal threshold, creating a formal and semantic restart. Hag.2.15-17 has a complete negative retrospective and failed-return conclusion; Hag.2.18-19 has a complete foundation-day hinge, inventory question, blessing reversal, and paragraph closure. Their larger shortfall-to-blessing unity remains mandatory retrieval context.

The explicit second same-day word and direct address govern the overthrow sequence and its servant-and-signet culmination through the final speech formula. The identity-sensitive close is not an independent literary unit.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Keep the doubled consider refrain, retrospective failure, foundation hinge, and blessing reversal as one surface unit.
preserved_dissents.evidence: The two halves form one shortfall-to-blessing reversal, no WLC-family paragraph marker follows Hag.2.17, and a samekh closes only after 2:19.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as the principal losing alternative; dependent children were selected because the repeated command and changed temporal threshold at 2:18 provide stronger local seam evidence.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Keep Hag.2.15-Hag.2.19 whole to protect the blessing reversal from isolated retrieval.
preserved_dissents.evidence: The blessing in 2:19 receives its force from the shortfall and failed return in 2:15-17, while paragraph closure occurs only after 2:19.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved; the selected children require mandatory Hag.2.15-Hag.2.19 hydration, so the retrieval concern remains operative.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Hag.1.12-Hag.1.14 plus a dependent Hag.1.15 date coda.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as a dependent internal seam; not selected because Hag.1.15 cannot stand independently.

preserved_dissents.evidence: The former-glory questions shift to threefold encouragement at Hag.2.4.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as an internal rhetorical seam; the question, exhortation, and reassurance remain one dated encouragement oracle.

preserved_dissents.evidence: The causal opening at Hag.2.6 grounds or continues the reassurance in 2:5.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as the mandatory parent relation; samekh after 2:5 and the renewed speech formula at 2:6 support two surface children.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Keep the priestly dialogue and retrospective blessing application as one dated surface unit.
preserved_dissents.evidence: No WLC-family paragraph marker follows Hag.2.14, and the retrospective beginning at 2:15 continues the same dated word event's application.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as the mandatory larger parent; the change from question-answer application to consider-and-retrospect form supports the local surface seam.

source_gaps: OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family views and cannot count as independent textual witnesses.
No authorized passage-pinned primary LXX, DSS, Targum, rabbinic, ANE, Persian-period, or Second-Temple packet was available.
The syntax of Hag.1.1-2, the date-coda relation at Hag.1.14-15, and the covenant-and-Spirit relation in Hag.2.5 remain translation-sensitive.
The temporal force of yet once more and the rendering and referent of the nations' desired or valuable things in Hag.2.6-7 remain unresolved.
The temporal direction and scope of the consider refrains in Hag.2.15 and Hag.2.18 remain translation-sensitive; the boundary ruling does not select a preferred English rendering.
The servant, signet, and election language in Hag.2.23 remains an identity and reception hot zone.
hold_assessment: No unresolved question presently prevents a boundary ruling. The principal Hag.2.15-2.19 dispute can be resolved by exposing the refrain-and-date-defined children while retaining mandatory parent hydration and the whole-unit dissent. Translation-sensitive questions lower confidence but do not require choosing a preferred reading, theology, chronology, or identity.
